For the purpose of this brochure, a "disclaimer" notice is defined as a statement placed

When is a Disclaimer Required?

Basic Rule

Individuals and Other Persons

A disclaimer must appear on any "electioneering communication" (defined below) and
on any public communication by any person that expressly advocates the election or
defeat of a clearly identified candidate or solicits funds in connection with a federal
election.

Definitions

Electioneering Communications

As defined in FEC regulations, an "electioneering communication" is a broadcast, cable
or satellite communication that fulfills each of the following conditions:
* Refers to a clearly identified federal candidate;
* Is publicly distributed within 30 days before a primary election or within 60 days before a general election; and

21 Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law. (Galatians 3:21 KJV)

Paul was making it clear that the law was not against the promises of God, but the law was not given to save people, or give life, but rather to give death (2 Corinthians 3:7). The law was perfect, but the problem was that we humans were, and are, not perfect, and therefore we could not, and cannot, keep the law perfectly (Romans 3:23). Then what was the purpose of the law? It was given to make sin come alive, and slow down the sin that was already in the world, until Jesus could come (Galatians 3:19). Jesus nailed the law to the cross He was crucified on (Colossians 2:14), and the law is no longer in effect, for those that are born again.

Many Churches are still teaching the law given through Moses. It is not wrong to teach the principals given in the law, as being the way that God desires us to live our lives, but it is entirely wrong to teach that we have to keep all, or any, of the law to be saved, or be right with God. God no longer looks on our performance, as He did under the law, but rather has given us His Grace, and does not hold our sins against us Christians as He did under the law. Where there is no law, sin is not imputed unto us (Romans 5:13). What a marvelous time we live in – the time of Grace. Thank you Lord, for not imputing our sins unto us anymore, and extending your mercy to us who believe in you, and obey you (Hebrews 5:9)!
